text:
Clouds Against Humanity

A small, cheap, locked-down DigitalOcean environment built with OpenTofu, applied by Spacelift, fed secrets by Doppler, and reachable only through Twingate. No droplet has a single public inbound port open. There is no VPN, no bastion host and no SSH on the internet.

It is a cloud extension of a homelab, and it exists to teach: this repository is the reference environment, and the lessons that use it live in the wiki.

 Start with the wiki
 
 The wiki is the real point of this project. Every lesson, flowchart, exercise and decision (including the ones that were wrong the first time) is written there; this repository is the environment those lessons use.
 
 - Wiki home : the map of everything.
 - Start here if you are new : cloud, Terraform and zero trust from zero.
 - Why this exists : where this comes from and who it is for.
 - Reading order : the paths, with time estimates.
 - Contents : every page once, grouped by theme, with what each is for.
 - Git from zero : if you have never used git.
 - Repository growth : stars, forks and weekly work, drawn from GitHub data; the as-of date is printed in the picture, and stars measure attention, not use.
 
 Who this assumes: a basic power user. You know how a computer works, may have built or repaired one, and have set up a router and done basic networking. If you could work a help desk or a retail repair counter, you can start; if not, IT 101 level material such as CompTIA A+ objectives is the benchmark (not an endorsement).
 
 Cost: the reading and the exercises are free and always will be, and nothing here is sold. Hands-on work uses your own accounts and your provider's bill, nothing you spend goes to the maintainer, and you choose what you can afford to run. The cost gates are explained in docs/cost.md. If you open a DigitalOcean account, my referral link is optional and nothing is gated behind it; the wiki says exactly what it is. The same pages are in docs/wiki/ if you prefer reading them in the repo.

 Found a mistake or have a question? Open an issue
 
 Something wrong, a command that failed, a confusing explanation, or a topic you wish was here? Please say so. Feedback is free, and it is how the lessons get better. Give feedback and open an issue walks through it for a first-timer. Never paste tokens, keys, account names, real IP addresses or hostnames, or anything that identifies you. Security problems go through SECURITY.md, not a public issue. See also CONTRIBUTING.md.

 Free, and not for sale

I grew up in a divorced home, struggling to find resources to level up my tech knowledge, and my whole career was built on second hand machines. My first brand new computer, a System76 Pangolin I still have, came roughly ten years in. If knowledge is power and getting to it costs money, then the power is only available to people who can afford it, and I refuse to be selfish and enrich myself by gatekeeping what everyone has a right to know. No bullshit, no "90K in 90 days" lies, no "you need this cert or degree." Just knowledge.

You can tip, donate or support me financially through Patreon, StreamElements or the cryptocurrency section, but you are under no obligation. The biggest way to support this project is to share it with everyone who needs it. The full version, including what I think of college and certs, is Why this is free and not for sale.

Recommending other springboards is encouraged throughout this project. The point is to get you thinking in different ways and outside the box, not to hand you one path to copy, so expect pages to point at things to try beyond what they cover.

 How it fits together

 

 
 Diagram source (Mermaid) 

 

 

 Piece Job Why this and not the obvious alternative 
 --- --- --- 
 Twingate (ZTNA) Gets an authenticated person to one specific host and port Connectors dial out, so nothing listens on the internet. A VPN would mean a public listener and network-wide access after one login. More 
 DigitalOcean Droplets, VPC, cloud firewalls Predictable pricing and a firewall that attaches by tag, so a droplet is protected from its first boot. More 
 OpenTofu Every resource as code, in layered stacks Open-source (MPL) Terraform fork; same language, no license surprise. More 
 Spacelift Runs plan and apply, holds state, waits for a human Nothing applies from a laptop or from CI, and pull request plans never see credentials. More 
 Doppler Holds every secret Spacelift holds one read-only token; nothing in this repo is a credential. More 
 GitHub Actions Tests, scanners, cost gate Calls hardened shared workflows, every action pinned by commit. More 

 Why not just a VPN?

Because a remote-access VPN authenticates you once and then puts your device on the network, and the box doing that authentication has to listen on the internet. Both halves of that have been the starting point of serious breaches: stolen credentials on a legacy single-factor VPN profile (Colonial Pipeline, 2021) and a long run of pre-authentication exploits in VPN appliances from Ivanti, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Citrix and Pulse Secure. ZTNA checks every connection against a per-resource policy and, as built here, leaves nothing listening at all.

That is not "VPNs are always wrong". WireGuard is a very different animal from an SSL VPN appliance, site-to-site tunnels are still fine, and ZTNA means trusting a vendor's control plane. The full argument, sources and the honest tradeoffs are on Why ZTNA and not a VPN .
